title: How do I use my ChatGPT credits?
author: Flag_Shagger
selftext:
I have like 5000 credits (approx. $200 worth) and I want to try making a simple game, but I don’t know where to begin. Earlier this year I used Gemini 3 Pro to make a simple dice rolling game inside Google AI Studio, and it was pretty fun. I want to use these credits but I don’t see how to use them on a free ChatGPT account. Secondly, how do I actually make the game so that I can actually “own” it locally instead of it being “inside” ChatGPT like my game was on Google AI studio? And finally is 5000 credits even enough to make a basic game? thx!

Sorry if these are dumb questions but it seems like everything on youtube is super advanced for a total noob :/

comments.author: Fizassist1
comments.body:
first, get the desktop app for gpt/codex.  then make a new folder you want your project in.  then make that project in codex and direct it to that folder.  

if youre like me and enjoy working in an engine for more freedom, I also recommend looking into godot.

and lastly, if you plan to work in 3d, download blender and hook the blender mcp up to your codex.

as far as how to do all of that, gpt chat can walk you through it.

replies.author: Flag_Shagger
replies.body: thank you very much, this is very helpful. chatgpt told me to use gadot, I don’t have any coding experience. If I’m understanding correctly, I should make an empty folder on windows, tell gpt to make me a game inside that folder, then open that folder in gadot to actually test the game, and then go back to gpt to ask it to change this or improve that, then go back to gadot and load the updated file…am I understanding correctly?

replies.author: HitMePat
replies.body: Yes you have the gist of it.  Just talk to GPT right in the codex app and tell you what it want.  "I want you to help me make a game that will be built in Godot.  This is the blank project folder.  Help me plan it out and get started, I have no idea how to even get started.  I want my game to be about _____".  And Codex/gpt will walk you through everything.  GPT can even launch your game in Godot for you right from the codex app for you to play test it, and make logs and event triggers so it can review your play tests so you can talk about it with him after.

replies.body: thank you so much dude, appreciate it! if you also have any tips please let me know, like for example which model to use

comments.author: Safe-Industry2465
comments.body:
I have my claude chat hooked up with an empty folder on my desktop and the Godot folder.

Now the chat has access to the godot files and can work on them.
Then I simply run the game from within Godot.

For my shop simulator game I just started very simple.

I told claude I want to build a shop simulator game in voxel graphics step by step and I want it to start with a simple shop, the ability to buy a shelf and healing potions. I told it that I wanted to be able to run around, order items, place them and that people can come and buy them.

Boom, simple(st) game loop.
From there I added things
- make a few more items
- let me set prices
- make different customers with different items they prefer
- let me level up by earning money. Let me buy upgrades for my shop e.g. faster item deliveries
- etc

From there I added "bigger" modules like
- let me be able to buy the tavern across the road. 
- let me unlock barkeepers and waiters that serve people
- etc etc

The game is now playable from end to finish. Its still shit, because I was vibe coding when I was high and my prompts were shit but still, it works and is expandable.
And it was daaaamn fun to build.

My approach had an issue, that the technical debt is creeping up.
Currently my claude is writing a GDD and refactoring the game though.

What I want to say though: just build something. Do it piece by piece, because it does not matter.
Your game and idea will be bad, but you will learn so much.

I for myself now know what is possible and will approach my next project with a little more care. But I learned that from my current project
